catalog_quote: L’accent en bribri tombe invariablement sur la dernière syllabe du morphème. Il se matérialise par une intensité plus importante et par un noyau vocalique moins bref que ne le sont les noyaux non accentués. ... Le système tonal du bribri oppose deux tons : haut vs descendant. L’opposition n’est attestée que dans les syllabes accentuées. Les syllabes non accentuées sont produites avec un ton bas par défaut. ... Les mots bribri étant souvent constitués de plusieurs morphèmes, plusieurs syllabes « accentuées » (syllabes finales de morphèmes) peuvent cohabiter au sein de cette unité. Dans ce cas de figure, souvent, une seule d’entre elles conserve son intensité et son ton distinctif. Les autres se réalisent généralement avec une intensité égale à celles des syllabes non accentuées, et le ton est neutralisé à moyen ou bas. sweep_summary: Bribri (brib1243) is in the catalog as 'morphological' (accent invariably on the morpheme-final syllable; two tones H vs falling contrast only in accented syllables) on Chevrier 2017. this search of works with stress in the title turned up a single title: Constenla Umaña 1985, 'Prosodic Nasality in Bribri (Chibchan) and Universals of Nasality', IJAL 51(4): 374-376 (DOI 10.1086/465898). It is a 2-page note on regressive nasal spreading, not on accent placement; every open route was tried (UChicago 403, JSTOR JS wall, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar closed with no repository copy, archive.org 0 hits, no archived copy at the Internet Archive), so it stays paywalled and unread; its bibliographic records are and. Chevrier 2017 (held) summarizes it: domain of nasal spread = word; it uses 'toniques' vs 'atones' syllables with the morpheme-final syllable the tonic one, and the p.375 forms Chevrier reproduces carry final stress — all consistent with the catalog's classification, so priority for acquisition is low. Verification done in this search of works with stress in the title: the catalog's deciding quotation is verbatim at line 5122 (sec. 2.6.1, p.93) of the Chevrier text we hold ('L'accent en bribri tombe invariablement sur la dernière syllabe du morphème..'), and the held Jara Murillo 2018 grammar sec. 2.3 p.22 independently states the same picture ('Wilson (1982: xix) caracteriza el bribri como una lengua de acento tonal.. "[e]n cada palabra no compuesta hay generalmente, sino siempre, un solo tono que funciona como acento en palabras de más de una sílaba".. las sílabas con vocal de tono bajo son inacentuadas' and 'La oposición tonal suele aparecer en sílaba final de morfema'). Both are already in the record, so no new first-hand stress statement was read and nothing supersedes Chevrier 2017. only direct downloads and API lookups were possible.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding passage (p.93, p.94, p.126, pp.217-218) is verbatim in the Chevrier 2017 text we hold at the stated locators. (2) Deciding source is a 2017 703-pp instrumental phonology dissertation — the most thorough description of Bribri prosody that exists per Glottolog and per Chevrier's own literature survey (all earlier phonological work is 8-19-pp sketches or pedagogical). The held Jara Murillo 2018 reference grammar (sec.2.3 p.22) independently gives the same picture: tonal accent, contrast normally on morpheme-final syllable, low-toned syllables unaccented, typically one accentual tone per word. The 'morphological' coding (accent = morpheme-final, demarcative, prefixes excepted, one primary per word with morpheme-final secondaries) is exactly what both sources state. (3) Nothing found on the web (no JIPA Illustration, no later Chevrier accent paper) would supersede
